extracted.intended_audience: media researchers, journalists, news executives, and policymakers interested in Spain's news ecosystem
extracted.subtask_description: A country-level profile summarising Spain's news ecosystem: audience metrics, advertising and subscription revenues, platform strategies, trust and press-freedom indicators, and technological and regulatory developments affecting journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population
rubrics_metrics.description: Population: 47 million
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic demographic context for interpreting audience and market size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet penetration
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet penetration: 93%
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key indicator of potential digital reach and online news adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media market characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Spanish media market is characterised by intense rivalries between major conglomerates, the continuing importance of broadcast news, and innovation online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative dimension used to describe competitive dynamics and where innovation is occurring (broadcast vs digital).

rubrics_metrics.name: Political, media and social polarisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Local and general elections in 2023 heightened political, media, and social polarisation, with news organisations covering the elections in a market defined by low media trust and decreasing interest in politics and information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual factor shaping news coverage and audience engagement; relevant when evaluating editorial framing and audience targeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear TV vs streaming viewing share
rubrics_metrics.description: Linear TV remains dominant, with 84% of viewing compared to 16% for streaming services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to assess the continuing importance of broadcast scheduling and the extent to which streaming has displaced traditional TV viewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: OTT subscription growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of Spaniards subscribing to OTT services has increased from 37% to 65% in the past five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator of streaming service penetration and audience migration to on-demand platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising revenue growth and digital share
rubrics_metrics.description: Spanish media companies experienced a modest increase in advertising revenue (4%) in 2023, with digital advertising accounting for 48% or €2.8bn of the €5.9bn total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad financial health metric; digital share highlights monetisation shift to online. Useful when evaluating business models for news organisations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital advertising distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital spending was primarily directed towards websites (38%), search engines (35%), and social media platforms (27%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows where advertisers allocate budgets online — relevant for platform strategy and commercial viability of different digital channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branded content growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Growth in branded content, up 21% to €550m, reflects how engaging and narrative-driven content has become a preferred method for connecting with audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals importance of sponsored/native content as a revenue stream and its increasing role in content strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format-specific ad revenue changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising revenues for magazines grew by 2.2% to €126m, fell in newspapers by 2.1% to €340m, and remained flat in TV (-0.2%) at €1.7bn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sector-by-sector performance metric to assess which formats are gaining or losing commercial traction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital news subscriptions (counts and audit caution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Company data indicate a total of 1.1 million digital subscribers. El País (350,000), El Mundo (123,000), and La Vanguardia (107,000) led this ranking. However, the lack of any independent audit of subscriber numbers means the figures should be viewed with caution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscription totals are an important measure of reader monetisation but the note about lack of independent audit is a data-quality caveat when using these numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organisational and editorial changes at broadcasters
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: Mediaset closed digital-born Nius and redeployed staff to Telecinco and Cuatro; Cuatro news bulletins restarted; Mediaset hired Carlos Franganillo as primetime anchor; turmoil at RTVE including board removal over a contract decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational and personnel changes indicate shifts in editorial strategy, stability, and political pressures affecting public and private broadcasters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform and social distribution strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Major Spanish news outlets have taken steps towards leveraging social platforms for wider news dissemination by distributing content through WhatsApp; Relevo pursues a vigorous social media strategy with >1 million followers and strong focus on TikTok and Twitch alongside Twitter and Instagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures the extent to which outlets prioritise social/distributed platforms for audience growth and engagement. Track presence and follower metrics on key platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative journalism impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevo's 2023 exposé of the sexual scandal involving Luis Rubiales became a huge story and eventually led to his resignation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrates the potential of investigative reporting to effect political/accountability outcomes — a qualitative performance benchmark for editorial impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and regulatory developments affecting platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: The Association of Information Media filed lawsuits against Meta alleging data protection violations and unfair competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as an indicator of friction between news organisations and tech platforms and as a factor shaping future platform compliance and revenue opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI adoption and editorial concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: 94% of Spanish media executives believe that AI will enhance user experiences through content personalisation. However, concerns about misinformation and the newsroom's capacity to adapt to AI-driven changes persist among Spanish editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dual-dimension metric: level of executive confidence in AI for personalisation, and residual editorial risk/skills gap. Important when evaluating technological strategy and newsroom preparedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust in news (overall and broadcaster-specific changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in news overall: 33%. Those who distrusted the news in general (40%) exceeded those who usually trusted it (33%). There was a 6 percentage-point increase in trust in the Spanish public broadcaster RTVE, driven by young adults (25–34) and voters on the left.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core audience sentiment metric; useful for assessing credibility and public perception of news outlets and for segment analysis (age, political leaning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paying for online news
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay for online news: 12%
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure of consumer willingness to pay — important for subscription-based revenue forecasting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Podcast listening
rubrics_metrics.description: Listen to podcast in the last month: 44%
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator of audio/audience engagement and potential for growth in audio journalism and advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press freedom ranking and score (RSF)
rubrics_metrics.description: RSF World Press Freedom Index: 30/180. Score 76.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International comparative indicator of press freedom used to situate the national environment for journalism and potential constraints on reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnoted data sources include the CNMC Household Panel (data.cnmc.es), Estudio Infoadex de la Inversión Publicitaria en España 2023, and IBERIFIER reports. Methodology section and downloadable PDF available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies provenance and allows assessment of data reliability and comparability; important when evaluating the robustness of reported metrics.
